title: Cryptarithm crackers
goal: I can find missing digits in sums and take-aways. I can solve magic squares and number pyramids.

learn.intro: In a missing-digit sum, work one column at a time. Start with the ones. Remember to add the digit you carried.

example.problem: Find the 2 missing digits in this sum.
steps: Tens: ? + 6 + 1 carried must end in 9. So ? is 2.

howto.title: How to find a missing digit
steps: Look at the ones column first.
Write the carried 1 above the next column.
For a take-away, turn it round and add to check.

try.explanation: Ones: 8 + 7 = 15, write 5 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. Hundreds: ? + 5 makes 9, so ? is 4. Thousands: 3 + 2 = 5.

items.text: Find the missing digit in each sum.
items.explanation: (a) Ones 6 + 1 = 7 and tens 4 + 5 = 9 are fine. Hundreds: ? + 2 = 5, so ? is 3. (b) Ones: 9 + 5 = 14, carry 1. Tens: ? + 3 + 1 ends in 0, so ? is 6 and 10 is made. Check: 2669 + 1435 = 4104.

items.text: Find the missing digit in each take-away.
items.explanation: Turn each one round and add. (a) 3687 + 2718 = 6405, so the digit is 7. (b) 4513 + 4617 = 9130, so the digit is 1.

items.text: A baker has 8000 g of flour. He uses 2475 g on Monday and 3150 g on Tuesday. How many grams of flour are left? {b} g
Siti works out 5000 - 1768 = 3342.
items.explanation: The check should give back 5000, but 3342 + 1768 = 5110. So Siti is not right. 5000 - 1768 = 3232. Check: 3232 + 1768 = 5000.

items.text: Look for a pattern.
items.explanation: (a) Each digit and its partner add up to 9: 2 and 7, 6 and 3, 4 and 5, 1 and 8. That gives 7358. (b) 10 000 is 1 more than 9999, so the answer is 1 more than 7358.

items.text: Every row, column and diagonal has the same total.
items.explanation: The middle row is complete: 550 + 350 + 150 = 1050. Top row: 200 + 450 + A = 1050, so A = 400. Left column: 200 + 550 + 300 = 1050. Middle column: 450 + 350 + B = 1050, so B = 250. Bottom row: 300 + 250 + C = 1050, so C = 500.

items.text: A brick is made by adding the 2 bricks below it.
items.explanation: P and 830 make the top brick: 830 + P = 1580, so P = 750. Q and 270 make P: Q + 270 = 750, so Q = 480. Check: 350 + 480 = 830.

parts.label: a

items.explanation: Ones: 2 + 6 = 8. Tens: 5 + ? ends in 4, so ? is 9 and 1 is carried. Hundreds: ? + 4 + 1 ends in 1, so ? is 6 and 1 is carried. Thousands: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Check: 3652 + 2496 = 6148.

items.text: Each letter stands for a digit. The same letter always means the same digit. Find the digit.
items.explanation: (a) Try A = 3: 33 + 23 = 56. It works. (b) Two equal numbers add up to 90, so each is 45. Then C = 4.

parts.label: a

items.text: The sum of 2 numbers is 9000. One number is 3475. What is the other number? {b}
Use the cards once each to make two 3-digit numbers.
items.explanation: For the greatest sum, put the 2 greatest digits in the hundreds places. Then the next 2 in the tens places, and the last 2 in the ones places: 800 + 700 + 50 + 40 + 3 + 2 = 1595. For the smallest sum, do the same with the smallest digits first: 200 + 300 + 40 + 50 + 7 + 8 = 605.

items.text:
Letters hide digits. The same letter is the same digit. Different letters are different digits.
AB + AC = BBD
items.explanation: Two 2-digit numbers make less than 200, so B = 1 and the answer starts 11. Ones: B + C = 1 + C ends in D. Tens: A + A + carry makes 11, so A = 5 with carry 1. Then 1 + C must be 10, so C = 9 and D = 0. Check: 51 + 59 = 110.
items.hint: Two 2-digit numbers add up to less than 200. What is B?

items.text: Use the cards 1, 3, 5, 6 and 8 once each. Make a 3-digit number and a 2-digit number. What is the smallest sum you can make? {b}
items.explanation: The smallest digit, 1, goes in the hundreds place. The next smallest, 3 and 5, go in the two tens places. The others, 6 and 8, go in the ones places. For example 136 + 58 = 194, and every way of placing the digits like this gives 194.
items.hint: Which digits are worth the least? Which places are worth most?

items.text: Look at this magic square. Every row, column and diagonal has the same total.
items.explanation: Add the middle row, the middle column and the 2 diagonals. The middle number is counted 4 times, and every other number once, so 4 totals = all 9 numbers + 3 times the middle number. All 9 numbers make 3 totals, so the total is 3 times the middle: 3 x 210 = 630. Then A = 630 - 120 - 270 = 240 and E = 630 - 120 - 210 = 300.
items.hint: The middle number is in 4 lines. Add those 4 lines.

items.text:
Letters hide digits. The same letter is the same digit. Different letters are different digits.
ABC + BC = CAB
items.explanation: Ones: C + C ends in B. Tens: B + B (+ carry) ends in A. Hundreds: A (+ carry) is C. Try C = 3: then B = 6, carry 0. Tens: 6 + 6 = 12, so A = 2 and carry 1. Hundreds: 2 + 1 = 3 = C. Check: 263 + 63 = 326. No other digits work.
items.hint: Look at the ones: C + C ends in B. List the choices for C.

items.text:
Beyond Level 3: Pyramids with a hidden number.
A brick is made by adding the 2 bricks below it. The 2 bricks marked X are equal. Find X. {b}
items.explanation: In this pyramid the end bricks of the bottom row count once in the top brick and the 2 middle bricks count 3 times each. So 200 + 3 X + 3 X + 440 = 3280. That is 640 + 6 X = 3280, so 6 X = 2640 and X = 440. Check: the next row is 640, 880, 880; then 1520, 1760; then 3280.
items.hint: Guess a number for X. Fill the pyramid. Is the top too big?

items.text:
Beyond Level 3: Reversing digits.
Reverse the digits of a 2-digit number and add the 2 numbers.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Each answer is in the {b} times table.

items.explanation: 99 = 9 x 11, 143 = 13 x 11, 121 = 11 x 11. Here is why. A 2-digit number with digits A and B is 10 A + B. Its reverse is 10 B + A. Together they make 11 A + 11 B, which is 11 x (A + B). So the answer is always in the 11 times table.
items.hint: Add the tens digit and ones digit. Compare with the answers.

items.text: Make up a number pyramid puzzle of your own. The bottom row has 3 bricks. Show exactly 3 bricks and hide the other 3, so that only ONE answer fits. Swap puzzles with a grown-up.

answer.text: Answers vary. Example: top brick 800, middle left brick 370, bottom right brick 180 shown. The hidden bricks are 430 (middle right), 250 (bottom middle) and 120 (bottom left).

items.explanation: Check that your pyramid adds up correctly and that the 3 shown bricks fix all the others. In the example: 800 - 370 = 430, then 430 - 180 = 250, then 370 - 250 = 120.
items.hint: Make a full pyramid first. Then hide 3 bricks.
